chapter_theme: A single song at Mayilam (மயிலம்): the poet, melting like wax before women's eyes, asks Murugan to come when Yama's messengers take his life; the praise turns on Murugan himself infatuated with the hunter girl and falling at her feet.

546.reading: The poet asks whether women's eyes are arrow or sword, poisoned spear or carp, fish or deer, and whether, overcome by their cuckoo speech, thread-thin waists and mountainous breasts, melting like wax in the forge and drowning in the sea of passion, he must perish by the disease of the body's five great sins; he asks that on the day Yama's messengers come shouting with club and noose to take his life, Murugan grant him his feet. The praise names the vel that dried the roaring sea and turned Sura's array to ash, the one who took another form, went into the hunters' forest, fell in love with the hunter girl and fell at her feet, the lord whose feet Sambhu worships, at the cool hill of Mayilam.
546.nuance: The opening is a riddle of comparisons (கோலோ வாளோ ... மீனோ மானோ), the familiar question of what the woman's eye is. The same word, மயல், describes Murugan's love for Valli (மயல்கொண்டு உலாய் அவள் தாள்மீதே வீழ்): the god's infatuation is praised in the song that confesses the poet's. உறுதண்ட பாசமொடு ஆரா வாரா is Death's men coming with club and noose, shouting.

links.note: Both open with a riddle of what a woman's eye is, a string of 'or's of weapons, poison and fish. In 103 Yama's messengers are one of the answers; 546 keeps them out of the list and sets them, with club and noose, at the end of the plea.

546 opens with the lover's riddle about the eye, கோலோ வாளோ வேலோ சேலோ மீனோ மானோ. Naladiyar 44 refuses the eyeless men who call eyes lilies, carp and spears (குவளை பொருகயல் வேல்) and sees a scooped-out palm fruit. The song voices the very comparisons the Naladiyar rejects, and then confesses where they led.

546 uses மயல் for the poet's lust and again for Murugan, who in love fell at the hunter girl's feet (மயல்கொண்டு உலாய் அவள் தாள்மீதே வீழ்). 309, at Kanchi, also gives the god's infatuation (அடிபணிந்திட்டப் பட்டு மயற்கொண்டு அயர்பவன்) while asking that the poet's own desire be quenched. Both set the god's praised mayal beside the poet's confessed one.

source_issues: Song 546: னு஡டே and கானு஡ டே have the corrupt glyph ஡ for ஊ (னூடே, கானூடே).
